title: fleet-build leg failing: build

labels.name: fleet-build-leg
labels.description: fleet-build variant: standing per-leg failure issue

body:
The gated fleet-build variant's **build** leg failed. This is the standing issue for this leg: later failures comment here instead of opening new issues, and the recovery is noted here too.

First failing run: https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41652341284

Error (step "Build :full (load locally, do not push yet)", cache export):

```
#19 ERROR: error writing layer blob: denied: installation not allowed to Write organization package
```

Filed manually: the variant's report job only tracks the warm-export legs (its `needs` and job-name filter exclude `build`), so this failure was not recorded automatically. Root cause and fix: PR #45 (merged) — the build job's layer-cache login used the repo `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which cannot write the organization package; the login now uses the `GHCR_ORG_PAT` classic PAT. A force re-dispatch follows the merge.

title: Optional warm-export legs fail silently inside green runs
body: Run 41600076443 completed SUCCESS while its warm-export (nix) leg failed in 8 seconds: the manifest names shell 'fleet' for nix, but the fleet repo's nix submodule pointer (6d02290f) predates dezren39/nix#1383, which added devShells.fleet — so the export errored with 'flake does not provide attribute devShells.x86_64-linux.fleet' and the manifest's 'optional' flag swallowed it. build-full and smoke passed; nothing for nix was realised or pushed. This is the third distinct false-green mode for this leg (after the cache-key skip, dezren39/fleet#30).\n\nFix the visibility, not just the instance (the pointer bump is a separate PR): an optional leg that errors should be impossible to miss in a green run — e.g. export.sh emits a workflow warning annotation and a step-summary table of per-leg outcomes (realised / cache-hit / FAILED-optional), and the smoke job lists which repos' closures the published image actually carries.

title: fleet-build: nar cache key ignores the manifest shell — shell changes silently keep warming the old shell
body:
Found 2026-11-03 while verifying the dezren39/nix fleet-shell fix (fleet#29 + dezren39/nix#1383): the publish run 41598906446 went green with warm-export (nix) in 49s — because the export step was SKIPPED on a nar-cache hit. The cache key is fleet-nar-<repo>-<flake.lock hash> only: it does not include which shell the manifest names. dezren39/nix's lock never changed, so the entry saved when the manifest said 'default' satisfied the run after the manifest switched to 'fleet' — the published :full still contains the default shell's closure, and the fleet shell has never actually been realised by the pipeline.

Same hazard for every repo: any future manifest shell change (or a repo adding/renaming its fleet shell) is silently ignored until the lock happens to change or a fresh_build is dispatched.

Fix: include the manifest's shell token for the repo in the nar cache key (fleet-nar-<repo>-<shell>-<lock hash>). First run after the fix re-exports everything once under honest keys — which is also the first true end-to-end test of nix's fleet shell.

title: fleet-build: build-full cache restores always miss (actions/cache version salt includes the restore path)
body:
Run 41556877450: all five warm-export jobs green, then build-full failed with 'required nar cache for code is missing or empty'.

Logs show warm-export (code) got 'Cache hit for: fleet-nar-code-b8fc...' (~648 MB) while build-full, minutes later in the same run, got 'Cache not found' for the identical key — for all five repos.

Root cause: actions/cache computes a cache *version* from the key PLUS the restore paths (and compression). The warm-export jobs save path `nar-cache`; build-full restores with path `restored/<repo>`. Different path → different version → permanent miss. Latent since the per-repo redesign (v3): no run had previously reached build-full with all exports green.

Fix: build-full restores every repo cache to the same path the exports save (`nar-cache`), merging into the build context after each restore, with the required-repo presence check applied per restore.

title: fleet-build export.sh: build stderr pollutes the captured store path, breaking nix copy
body:
Found in publish run 41550950349 (per-repo warm-export v3): the opencode and openchamber jobs realised their shells fine, then failed at the copy step with `error: stack overflow (possible infinite recursion)`.

Root cause: export.sh captures the build result with

```bash
out=$(nix build ... --print-out-paths "$dir#devShells..." 2>&1)
```

The `2>&1` folds substitution progress (`copying path ... from 'https://cache.nixos.org'`) into `$out`, so `nix copy --to file://... "$out"` receives a multi-line blob instead of one store path. Repos whose builds printed nothing to stderr (nix, zettel) were unaffected, which is why this survived several runs.

Fix: capture stdout only for the path; send stderr to a per-repo log file and print its head on failure (preserving the existing failure-head behaviour).

title: fleet-run (developing-today/fleet): legs fail checkout — "Input required and not supplied: token" when the checkout token resolves empty
body:
## Defect

`fleet-run.yml` in **developing-today/fleet** fails every leg whose checkout token resolves empty: the "Check out the target repo" step passes `token: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}` to `actions/checkout@v4` unconditionally, and checkout hard-fails on an empty token instead of checking out the (public) target anonymously.

(Filed on dezren39/fleet because developing-today/fleet — the fork whose workflow this is — has issues disabled.)

## Evidence

- Run [41842327372](https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/41842327372) (fleet-run, dispatched as the `developing.today` app; single leg targeting dezren39/fleet, command `git rev-parse HEAD && echo fleet-run-smoke-ok`).
- Setup job: **success** — inputs resolved correctly, target dezren39/fleet, run head was the fleet-place merge `05fd2b7e`.
- Run leg `run (dezren39/fleet #0)`: "Validate inputs" passed, then "Check out the target repo" failed:

  ```
  ##[error]Input required and not supplied: token
  ```

- In that run the `secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT` expression resolved to an empty string in the leg (the run was dispatched at 13:54Z; the fork's `GHCR_ORG_PAT` secret was provisioned minutes later during G3, at 13:57:54Z). Regardless of provisioning timing, the workflow has no safe state when the token is empty: an unconditional `token:` input turns a missing/unprovisioned secret into a hard failure even for public targets.
- The together-mode clone step has the same exposure: it interpolates `CLONE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GHCR_ORG_PAT }}` into every clone URL unconditionally.

## Reference fix (proven pattern)

developing-today/code's `org-run.yml` solves exactly this with an auth split: token checkout only for the repos its token covers, anonymous `git clone` (same depth/ref semantics) for public repos — it never passes an empty token input.

Apply the same pattern to developing-today/fleet's `fleet-run.yml`:

- Decide checkout auth per leg from whether a token is actually available, never emit an empty `token:` input.
- Public targets (all five allowlisted fleet repos are public; dezren39/fleet in particular) must check out cleanly with or without a usable PAT.
- Together legs: token URL only when a token is available, anonymous URL otherwise.

## Acceptance

- The identical smoke (single leg, dezren39/fleet, `git rev-parse HEAD && echo fleet-run-smoke-ok`) dispatched as the app concludes **success**, verified from the run log: printed SHA = current dezren39/fleet main head, marker line `fleet-run-smoke-ok` present.

title: fleet-build smoke: offline shell step dies on code@main flake.lock drift + root-owned checkout
body:
Surfaced by the #28 verification run [41834923394](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/41834923394) (2026-11-04). The gating did its job — every job executed — but smoke's `Warmed shell opens OFFLINE` step failed inside its test subject:

- Smoke checks out developing-today/code @ main (44b2dd56) and runs `nix develop .#fleet --offline` as vscode in the published :full container.
- During evaluation, nix tried to UPDATE code's flake.lock: input `openchamber/opencode` resolved from `github:developing-today-forks/opencode/4175c630` (2026-11-03, as locked) to `github:developing-today/opencode/ce1aec22` (2026-11-04) — code's flake inputs drifted during today's fork reorganization, so the committed lock no longer matches the flake's resolution.
- Writing the updated lock then failed: `error: opening file ".../code-check/flake.lock": Permission denied` — the checkout is root-owned and nix runs as vscode (the safe.directory fix earlier in the step covers git reads, not lock writes).

Two candidate fixes (either or both):
1. Make the smoke checkout writable by vscode (chown the code-check tree, like other steps do), so a lock refresh cannot die on permissions — though an `--offline` smoke arguably should not be refreshing locks at all.
2. Pin smoke to the same code rev the warm-export leg realised (the committed submodule pin / cache key basis) instead of floating on code's current main, so the smoke tests exactly what was warmed.

Pre-existing environment/subject drift, not a pipeline gating defect: the last fully green runs were 2026-11-03, before code's inputs moved. Filed from the #28 verification pass per fleet practice.

title: fleet-build publish: an optional export leg's hard job death blocks build-full + smoke
body:
Run 41564555311 (fresh_build dispatch, 2026-11-03): the optional warm-export (nix) job died abruptly mid-step at 2h02m (step 8 stuck in_progress, logs never uploaded — BlobNotFound; runner/container killed, consistent with resource exhaustion on dezren39/nix's oversized default shell). Because build-full has needs: warm-export (the whole matrix), the job failure skipped build-full and smoke, failing the publish — even though all three REQUIRED repos (code, opencode, openchamber) exported fine and their caches were complete.

The graceful path works (an optional export STEP failure is continue-on-error, so the job succeeds); only a hard job death exposes this. The real required-repo guard already exists inside build-full: the merge step hard-fails if a required repo's nar cache is missing or empty.

Proposed fix: give build-full (and smoke, transitively) an if: ${{ !cancelled() }} so a failed optional matrix leg cannot block the publish, relying on the merge step's required-repo checks as the gate. The 60-minute warm-export timeout added in PR #27 already halves the bleed on a repeat (122 min -> 60), but the publish should not depend on optional legs at all.

title: Reject missing or extra gitlinks before planning umbrella verification
body:
The umbrella verification plan at 95d6c5da joins declared paths to gitlinks before checking coverage. When a declared path lacks a gitlink the jq join emits no row. A gitlink with no matching declaration is also ignored. This can leave a successful plan that silently omits a member. The README also maintains a partial roster while FLEET.md already lists the 22 members and their management tiers.

Aster is taking this narrowly scoped follow-up for developing-today/code#13272. Compare the full mode-160000 tree with the independently declared paths before producing any legs. Preserve recorded-only private handling. Exercise matched, missing, and extra paths against local synthetic Git metadata on a GitHub-hosted runner. Point the README at the canonical roster and describe Codespaces initialization separately.

title: sync-upstream: developing-today/fleet main has diverged from upstream
body: The daily sync-upstream run in developing-today/fleet hit a merge conflict pulling dezren39/fleet main, aborted the merge, and pushed nothing. Run: https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/44900082037. Commits belong upstream in dezren39/fleet; this fork's main needs a manual convergence.

title: replicate: format auto-fix workflow (auto-format) from developing-today/code PoC (#2015)
body:
Replicate the format auto-fix workflow proven in developing-today/code (PoC: developing-today/code#2015) to this repo.

**PoC evidence (verified 2026-11-14 on code@main):**
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/auto-format.yml` in developing-today/code — scheduled treefmt pass, `cancel-in-progress: false` concurrency, `AUTO_FORMAT_LAST_SUCCESS_SHA` success/loop guard, bot pushes directly to main.
- Run https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43629197226 (success, 2026-11-14T22:44:22Z) formatted 356 changed files and pushed bot commit https://github.com/developing-today/code/commit/8fb88d0b1d176e48038a59964a3ae7e8bd6e39bf (`style(treefmt): auto-format on main`, github-actions[bot]) — misformatted files on main corrected with no human touch and no loop (single bot commit; next main commit is a human merge).

**Scope for this repo**
- Census tier for this repo (per developing-today/code#2017 census, tiers accepted by Drew under developing-today/code#2230, decisions ledger fleet-tiers-2230, answered 2026-11-14): Umbrella-only — census recommendation accepted under #2230; this repo is the fleet umbrella itself. Census point 5 (#2017): each added repo joins the #2015 format auto-fix replication set once the PoC lands.
- Adapt, don't blind-copy: use this repo's own formatters / treefmt (or equivalent) config; keep the PoC's invariants — (1) formatting never gates a merge, (2) a pass is never cancelled mid-commit, (3) a success marker / equivalent guard prevents re-processing and loops, (4) bot commits go directly to the default branch with a clear `style(treefmt): auto-format on main` (or repo-equivalent) message.
- If this repo has no meaningful formattable sources, close this issue with that evidence instead of adding an empty workflow.

**Acceptance**
- A deliberately misformatted file committed to the default branch is corrected by the workflow with no human touch and no loop, with the workflow run / bot commit linked on this issue.

Parent: developing-today/code#2015. Decision: developing-today/code#2230 (census recommendations accepted 2026-11-14).
